bib.title: Is ChatGPT better than Human Annotators? Potential and Limitations of ChatGPT in Explaining Implicit Hate Speech

question: Can ChatGPT detect implicit hateful tweets and generate natural language explanations (NLEs) of quality comparable to human-written ones?
contributions: Prompt design eliciting concise ChatGPT classification plus NLE for implicit hate
MTurk user studies comparing ChatGPT and human-written NLEs on informativeness and clarity

method.summary: 795 LatentHatred implicit-hate tweets were sent to ChatGPT three times each with a one-sentence-explanation prompt; yes/no answers were aggregated into a score. Disagreement cases were re-labelled by MTurk workers under three contexts, and 100 tweets had NLEs rated for informativeness and clarity.
method.task: implicit hate classification and natural language explanation generation

datasets.name: LatentHatred (ElSherief et al. 2021)
datasets.split: random 12.5% (795), equal to the test size for explanation generation in the original; 100 sampled for NLE quality rating

inference.samples: 3 responses per tweet, new chat session per tweet
inference.prompting: zero-shot single prompt; unofficial ChatGPT API (github.com/acheong08/ChatGPT)

parameters.aggregation: Yes=+1, No=-1, other=0; mean of 3 = ChatGPT score; >0 Hateful, <0 Non-Hateful, 0 Uncertain

metrics.name: Informativeness
metrics.definition: MTurk 7-point Likert, relevance of NLE in explaining why tweet is hateful

metrics.name: Clarity
metrics.definition: MTurk 7-point Likert, how clear the NLE is

metrics.name: average hatefulness score
metrics.definition: mean of three MTurk labels, Yes=+1, No=-1, Not Sure=0

eval.protocol: MTurk Masters (approval >98%, >5000 HITs, US); 3 workers per item; research assistants reviewed and resolved disputes for NLE ratings; t-tests; no demographics collected; no inter-annotator agreement reported

prompts.text: Given Post: ‘An Implicit Hateful Tweet’. Answer yes or no for whether the post is implicitly hateful. Explain why in one sentence.

results.claim: ChatGPT labels 80% of implicit hate tweets as hateful, agreeing with the dataset labels.
results.setup: LatentHatred implicit-hate tweets, ChatGPT Jan 9 2023 version, prompt: classify + one-sentence explanation
LatentHatred implicit-hate tweets, ChatGPT Jan 9 2023 version, prompt: classify + one-sentence explanation
results.quote: ChatGPT recognizes 146 instances as ‘Not Implicitly Hateful (18.4%)’

results.claim: Clarity of ChatGPT NLEs is higher than human-written NLEs.
results.setup: LatentHatred implicit-hate tweets, ChatGPT Jan 9 2023 version, prompt: classify + one-sentence explanation; 100 random tweets, 3 ratings each
results.quote: ChatGPT-generated NLEs show significantly higher Clarity scores (mean: 5.39) than human-written NLEs (mean: 4.68)

results.claim: Informativeness shows no significant difference between ChatGPT and human NLEs.
results.setup: LatentHatred implicit-hate tweets, ChatGPT Jan 9 2023 version, prompt: classify + one-sentence explanation; 100 tweets
results.quote: there is no statistically significant difference in Informativeness (t(198) = -0.69, p = 0.49)

results.claim: With post only, MTurk workers lean non-hateful on disagreement cases.
results.setup: 159 disagreement cases (146 not hateful + 13 uncertain), post only
results.quote: we find the average hatefulness score is negative (mean: -0.41)

results.claim: With the ChatGPT NLE, workers lean even more non-hateful.
results.quote: the average hatefulness score is negative (mean: -0.52) when a post is given with the ChatGPT-generated NLE
results.note: Difference vs post only: t(316) = -13.75, p<0.001

results.claim: With the human-written NLE, workers lean hateful.
results.quote: the average hatefulness score is positive (mean: 0.29)

limits: Short 4-page study; one prompt, one ChatGPT version, one dataset; no prompt variants tested (authors defer)
Disagreement cases are judged by lay MTurk workers, not experts; no agreement statistics reported
Unofficial API, no temperature or decoding settings, no code or data release stated
Authors concede ChatGPT NLEs can reinforce lay perception and mislead if wrong
Only 100 tweets rated for NLE quality; one NLE randomly chosen of three
Informativeness not shown higher, so the title's 'better than' holds only for clarity
146+13 = 159 disagreements, but t-test df 316 implies ~317 paired items
